column4: The gloss "pertaining" is vague and incomplete, and the sense of pertaining to real numbers is already covered by another meaning, so this entry is a duplicate.
Hollander is a noun (a person from Holland), not an adjective, and the gloss "of" is meaningless; the adjective form is "Hollands", so this meaning does not exist.
The gloss "one's" is not a meaning of "schors" (bark, crust); the real senses are already covered by the other meanings, so this entry is spurious.

The gloss "less commonly" is not a translation, and the meanings it could stand for (wreath of roses, rosary) are already listed, while the plant, youth and virginity senses are not real senses of rozenkrans, so this entry is a duplicate or invalid.
Marker is not an adjective in Dutch (it is a noun meaning marker pen or a place name), and the gloss "of" is meaningless, so this adjective meaning does not exist.
The gloss "someone" is wrong for "lelijkheid", which means ugliness or unpleasant behaviour, both already covered by the other meanings, so this entry should be removed.
The gloss "in" is wrong for Perzisch, and the only valid meaning, "Persian", is already listed as another meaning, so this entry is a bad duplicate.
By analogy is not a meaning of "bef"; it looks like a stray sense from a different entry, and the real senses (collar tabs, vulva, etc.) are already covered by the other meanings.
In particular is not a meaning of beunhaas, which means a bungler or unlicensed amateur tradesman, so this entry is wrong and the real senses are already covered.
Diemer is a proper-noun-derived form (relating to Diemen or the Diemermeer), not a real archaic adjective meaning "of", and with no other meanings or example there is nothing to salvage.
The gloss "in" is wrong and meaningless for IJslands, and the only valid meaning, Icelandic, is already listed as another meaning, so this entry is a duplicate.
The gloss "in" is wrong for Laotiaans, and the only valid sense, "Laotian", is already listed as another meaning, so this entry is a bad duplicate.
The gloss "in" is wrong for Oost-Vlaams, and the only valid sense, "East Flemish", is already listed as another meaning, so this entry is a bad duplicate.
The gloss 'someone' is not a real separate meaning of stiefkind, which only means stepchild, already listed as another meaning.
Veers is not a standard Dutch adjective (it is at most a rare, obscure form such as a Frisian or place-related word), and the gloss "of" is meaningless, so this entry should be removed.
The adverb 'aan' has no meaning of 'growth'; the example uses 'aan' as a preposition in 'bijdragen aan', and 'groei' only carries the idea of growth.
The meaning 'equal' duplicates the other listed meaning 'even' (as in an even number or level), and the example actually shows the adverb 'even' (equally), not an archaic adjective.
To get hooked is not a meaning of helpen, and the example just shows the ordinary sense "to help", which is already listed.
The meaning 'plenty' is essentially the same as the existing 'enough' meaning of genoeg, and the example actually just illustrates 'enough', so this is a duplicate.
onder does not mean "during" (that would be "tijdens"), and the example actually illustrates the "under" meaning, which is already listed.
Bijna means 'almost' or 'nearly', not 'soon', so this meaning duplicates the existing 'almost' sense and the example is better translated as 'My birthday is almost here'.

Krijgen does not mean "to wage war" (that would be "voeren" or the archaic "krijgen" only in "oorlog krijgen" meaning to get war), and the example actually uses the ordinary meaning "to get/receive", which is already covered by another meaning.
Movie sector is not a distinct meaning of film; it duplicates the existing "film production" meaning and the example just shows the ordinary "film" sense.
The example actually shows the meaning 'to require' (already listed), and 'to demand' is a duplicate of it rather than a distinct sense of vragen.

om te is a conjunction-like construction introducing an infinitive, and this meaning "to" duplicates the existing "in order to" meaning; the example is the "too ... to" construction, not a separate adverb sense.
This meaning 'once again' duplicates the other meaning 'yet again', and the example is a correct use of 'nog eens' as 'once more', so there is no distinct sense to keep.
te is not an article, and the 'in idiom' meaning is not a real sense; the example just uses the ordinary infinitive particle "te" and does not illustrate an archaic article.
The letter 't' does not mean 'tower', and the example uses 't as a contraction of 'het', not the noun 'de t' (the letter), so this meaning does not exist.
But then is not a separate sense of conjunction "maar"; the example is just a plain contrastive "but", so it duplicates the existing "but"/"yet" meanings.
The noun 'wel' means a spring or well, so 'shaft' is not a real meaning of it and 'well' is already listed as another meaning.
The gloss 'doing well!' is just a weaker duplicate of the other meaning 'well done!', so this entry adds nothing.
wie is an interrogative/relative pronoun meaning "who", not a noun, and the entry has a non-translation gloss ("Wie") and no example, so this noun meaning does not exist.

Dutch "door" is a preposition/adverb ("through, by"), and "de door" meaning "fool" does not exist as a Dutch noun (it resembles the English word "dour" or an archaic Germanic form), so this entry is invalid.
The Dutch word is "de man", not "het man"; there is no neuter noun "man" meaning this, so the entry is ungrammatical and has no valid meaning.
The meaning 'callus' does not exist for 'het weer'; it looks like a mismatch with another word, and the other senses listed (weather, wether, etc.) are separate or unrelated.
Foxing (in textiles) is not a recognised meaning of Dutch "het weer", which is mainly weather, so this looks like a wrong or dubious sense from a bad source.
het weer means weather; "knot in wood" is not a meaning of this word (that would be "de kwast" or "het knoest"), so this entry is wrong.
The meaning 'seisin' does not exist for Dutch 'weer' (it looks like a mistaken or obscure entry), and the listed meanings already cover the real senses.
Wether (a castrated ram) is not a meaning of the Dutch noun "weer" (that would be "hamel" or "ram"), so this sense is spurious.
Dag does not mean "meeting" in Dutch; the noun means day or daytime, so this meaning does not exist.
The Dutch word 'dag' does not mean 'piece of rope'; this meaning does not exist for the word.
Separated is essentially the same meaning as the other listed senses "split up" and "broken up", so it duplicates them.
Helemaal means 'completely' or 'entirely', not 'especially' (that would be vooral), and the meaning is not one that helemaal has apart from the existing 'completely' sense.
The noun 'gek' means a fool or madman, and 'cowl on a chimney' is not a meaning of it (that would be 'kap' or 'schoorsteenkap'), so this meaning does not exist.
'bang' is not a standard Dutch noun meaning 'sharp'; the adjective is 'bang' meaning 'afraid', and the noun sense is not established, so this meaning does not exist as listed.
o is not a Dutch adjective meaning "neutral"; it is a letter or interjection ("o"), so this adjective meaning does not exist.
The meaning 'mass' duplicates the existing 'pile' and 'multitude' senses of 'hoop' (as in 'een hoop mensen'), so it adds nothing as a separate entry.
